annotation:
I was born and raised in the small seaside town of Seabrook, nestled along the rugged coastline of Maine. My parents were both teachers, and they instilled in me a deep love for learning and exploration. From a young age, I could always be found with my face buried in a book, devouring stories of far-off lands and fantastical creatures. When I wasn't reading, I spent hours wandering the rocky shorelines, collecting sea glass and daydreaming about the adventures that awaited me beyond the horizon.

As I grew older, my curiosity and passion for discovery led me to pursue a degree in marine biology at the University of New England. Throughout my undergraduate years, I became increasingly fascinated by the intricate relationships between oceanic ecosystems and their inhabitants. During my junior year, I had the opportunity to participate in an expedition to study the complex behaviors of humpback whales off the coast of Nova Scotia. It was there, amidst the vast expanse of the Atlantic Ocean, that I discovered my true calling - using the knowledge and skills I had acquired to help protect and preserve our planet's precious marine habitats.

Upon graduation, I was accepted into a prestigious master's program at the University of British Columbia, where I focused on developing innovative conservation strategies for endangered coral reef systems. My research took me to the crystal-clear waters of the Great Barrier Reef, where I worked closely with renowned marine scientists and local communities to better understand the impacts of climate change and human activities on these fragile ecosystems. Through hands-on experience and rigorous academic training, I gained a profound appreciation for the delicate balance that exists within our natural world, and the crucial role we must play in maintaining it.

After completing my master's degree, I joined a leading environmental nonprofit organization as a marine conservation specialist. In this role, I collaborate with international partners to develop and implement sustainable practices in coastal communities, safeguarding the health of our oceans while also supporting the wellbeing of those who depend on them. Whether I'm working with local fishermen to adopt eco-friendly fishing methods, conducting workshops on ocean literacy, or advocating for policy changes that prioritize conservation efforts, I am driven by the belief that every person has the power to make a difference.

Outside of my professional pursuits, I continue to nurture my lifelong love for learning and exploration through travel, literature, and art. I find inspiration in the beauty and complexity of the world around me, drawing connections between seemingly disparate realms and seeking to understand the underlying patterns that govern our existence. And though my journey has taken me far from the quiet shores of Seabrook, I remain forever grounded in the lessons and values that shaped me, grateful for the opportunities I've been given and committed to making a positive impact on the world I inhabit.
